task: open-tennis-robots (flagship row 6, buildable item): why the jittery tach does worse through a speed change

errors.what: Ran the first diagnostic in the foreground with a 110 s timeout; one drill takes about 2-3 min, so it was killed with nothing written
First truncation metric (last tick edge minus snapshot length) counted ticks logged after the snapshot as lost periods, so it looked like a ring overflow
errors.fix: measured the snapshot's own length instead: 103 periods at most, under the 128 ring; hypothesis rejected

doc_friction.issue: The pkill hint ('[n]ame' bracketed) is not enough: the hook also refuses when the same name appears unbracketed elsewhere in the command line; kill <pid> was the way out.

writeups: ventures/open-tennis-robots/firmware/esp32/README.md ('The jittery tach through a speed change')
notes: Hypotheses tested: (1) the speed change biases the drop, (2) the 128-period tach ring truncates through-change snapshots, (3) chance from shifted jitter draws. (2) rejected on the worst build (max snapshot 103 periods both modes). Six seeds x 6 builds x hold/through on the 3 us jitter plant (72 drills, 3,888 wheels, none aborted): wheels >2% off 35 hold vs 38 through; per seed 3/8, 7/7, 5/5, 5/8, 8/4, 7/6; paired mean |err| through minus hold -0.019 points over 1,944 pairs. Misses cluster on the fast partner wheel of a slow (watched) shot in both modes (5.1%/5.5% past 2%, sd 1.00%), vs 0.3%/0.5% (sd 0.6%) for a fast shot's wheels; slow wheels 0 of 360 past 2% in either mode. No firmware change. Spin-fit errors were not rerun across seeds (stated in README). Verification: check_post_frontmatter, check_post_links, post_similarity, portfolio/router/validate.py, run_venture_tests.py open-tennis-robots (see PR).
